messages:
Alex K: Quick sync — planning apples-to-apples load tests for the quant/speculative decode experiments. Goal: measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and quality delta vs fp16 baseline. Proposed approach: run synthetic and replay harnesses and lock infra variables.

Cheng L: SGTM. Two parallel harnesses: synthetic (rps-driven) and replay (real traces). Keep batcher config identical across runs.

Maya R: Important: kernel selection must be fixed for each run (no auto-select) so we compare kernel A vs B directly.

Jordan S: +1. Also need KV cache warmup script. If KV miss rate differs that will skew token latency.

Alex K: Draft loadtest config (for discussion):
```
clients: 200
qps: 500
seq_len: 256
model: my-model-v2
batcher:
  max_batch_size: 32
  max_latency_ms: 20
quant_profiles: [fp16, int8_dynamic, q4f16]
speculative: [off, 1.2x, 1.5x]
```

Cheng L: For apples-to-apples, pin: kernel_version, cudnn/cuBLAS flags, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, model weights checksum, and environment vars. Also capture kernel selection log.

perf-bot: CI run queued: run/bench-1742001250 (will post artifacts here when done)

Maya R: Regression gate proposal: max 3% QoR drop (per eval suite) or else fail. Perf promotion: require >=10% token/sec improvement and no >5% increase in p95.

Jordan S: How do we measure QoR? Offline eval set + 5 targeted prompts. Use identical seeds for sampling and the same decode params.

Alex K: Agreed. Also include KL/ROUGE/chrF metrics and a tiny human-blind subset for high-risk prompts.

Cheng L: A note on KV: run cold-start + steady-state. Cold-start = empty KV; steady-state = warm with 1000 prefixes (replay traces). Log KV hit/miss and average cache size.

Maya R: For batching heuristics, run at three QPS points: low/regime/saturation (100, 500, 1200) and dump batch-size distribution histograms.

Jordan S: On profiling, capture NVTX + wallclock + per-op counters. We'll need kernel-level timings to spot kernel selection regressions and contention.

Alex K: Action items: Cheng create replay-harness job with deterministic seed; Maya author loadtest config in infra repo; Jordan add KV warmup script and profiler hooks; I'll draft regression gate YAML and test criteria.

Cheng L: I'll spin up a run today and post the initial perf numbers. Tagging the replay trace subset `customer-telemetry-2026-q1`.

perf-bot: run/bench-1742001250 completed. Artifacts: https://ci.example/bench/1742001250

Alex K: Thanks — will pull results and look for oddities. If p95 regresses more than 10% we'll triage kernel selection + batcher logs first.

Maya R: FYI: speculative decoding often improves throughput but can amplify tail latency. Add a tail-latency SLA check (p99/p99.9).

Jordan S: Also test mixed-precision (fp16 kernels) vs quant kernels: sometimes int8 loses on long sequences because of accumulated numeric error in KV.

Cheng L: First pass numbers (synthetic + replay median):
- int8_dynamic: +18% tokens/sec, p95 +9% (regression)
- q4f16: +12% tokens/sec, p95 +2% (acceptable)
- speculative 1.5x: +30% tokens/sec, p95 +22% (unacceptable tail)

Alex K: Good initial data. Let's isolate kernel selection by forcing kernels (force_kernel="xla_fast" vs force_kernel="reference") and rerun the worst-case trace to see where latency jumps.

Maya R: I'll open a follow-up thread with the regression triage notes and attach NVTX flamegraphs.

Jordan S: +1 — also include batcher queue depth and per-batch token counts so we can correlate p95 with batching behavior.

Alex K: Thanks all :thumbsup:
